sentences.text: Zhyrasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph known only from fragmentary fossils, including a frontal bone from the roof of the skull.
The genus Zhyrasuchus was described in 1989 by Lev Nessov and colleagues.
Zhyrasuchus is classified within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
Zhyrasuchus is tentatively classified in the family Crocodylidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Zhyrasuchus as Crocodylidae.
Fossils of Zhyrasuchus were found in the Coniacian-age Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation in Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan.
Zhyrasuchus lived during the Turonian stage of the Cretaceous, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.

A 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov could not determine the relationship between Zhyrasuchus and the contemporary Tadzhikosuchus, or if they were synonyms, due to the scarcity of fossil material.
